data simulation
```{python}
# Set randomization seed
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

# Specify a function to simulate data
# predictors: snow making (in), # of days open last year, # of runs at the resort, avg snow fall(in)
def sim_data(n, beta_0, beta_snow_making, beta_days_open_last, beta_runs, beta_avgsnow, sigma):
    
    snow_making = rng.normal(2, 700, size=n).clip(min=0)
    days_open_last = rng.normal(45, 165, size=n).clip(min=0)
    runs = rng.normal(13, 195, size=n).clip(min=1)
    avgsnow = rng.normal(165, 136, size=n).clip(min=0)
    error = rng.normal(0, sigma, size=n)

    sentiment_latent = ( #creating the sentiment function
        beta_0
        + beta_snow_making * snow_making
        + beta_days_open_last * days_open_last
        + beta_runs * runs
        + beta_avgsnow * avgsnow
        + error
    )
    sentiment = np.clip(np.round(sentiment_latent), 1, 7)  # editing sentiment_latent to fit the model to the 7-point scale
    return sentiment, snow_making, days_open_last, runs, avgsnow, error

sentiment, snow_making, days_open_last, runs, avgsnow, error = sim_data( # run coefficients based on simulation estimates
    n=240, beta_0=-1.0, beta_snow_making=0.002, beta_days_open_last=0.02,
    beta_runs=0.015, beta_avgsnow=0.002, sigma=0.8
)

# create dataframe for storage
df = pd.DataFrame({
   "sentiment": sentiment,
    "snow_making": snow_making,
    "days_open_last": days_open_last,
    "runs": runs,
    "avgsnow": avgsnow,
    "error": error
})

print (df.head())
```

sim data model fitting
```{python}
#model fitting 
fr_fit = smf.ols ( 
    "sentiment ~ 1 + snow_making + days_open_last + runs + avgsnow + state", data = df).fit()

#Display regression results 
print(fr_fit.summary())
```

```{python}
# check for representativeness 
snow_data_train = snow_data.to_dummies(columns=['state'], drop_first = False).select(pl.exclude(['state_Nevada','state_New England','state_NorthernCalifornia','state_Oregon','state_SierraNevada','state_SierraNevada','state_SouthernCalifornia','state_Utah']))
```


```{python}
#fit the model 
# Get all state dummy columns
state_cols = [col for col in snow_data_train.columns if col.startswith('state_')]

# formula for our model 
formula = 'sentiment ~ 1 + Q("Snow Making") + daysOpenLastYear + Runs + averageSnowfall + ' + ' + '.join([f'Q("{col}")' for col in state_cols])

# fit model 
fit_01 = smf.ols(formula, data=snow_data_train).fit()
print(fit_01.summary())
```


```{python}
# Save the dffits values
snow_data_train = (snow_data_train
  .with_columns(dffits = fit_01.get_influence().dffits[0])
  .with_columns(abs_dffits = pl.col('dffits').abs())
  .with_row_index('observation02')
)
```


```{python}

# independence

(ggplot(
        snow_data_train,
        aes(x = 'observations', y = 'residuals')
      )
      + geom_line(alpha = 0.5)
      + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = 'red')
      + labs(
        title =
          'Independence: Sequential Residuals',
        subtitle =
          'Look for a trend in mean or variance'
      )
    )
```


```{python}
# constant variance
(ggplot(
        snow_data_train,
        aes(
          x = 'residuals_01',
          y = 'fitted_values_01'
        )
      )
      + geom_point(alpha = 0.25, color = 'red')
      + labs(
        title =
          'Constant Variance: Residuals vs. Fitted Values',
        subtitle =
          'Look for a funnel shape in the residuals'
      )
    )
```


```{python}
# Normality
(ggplot(
        snow_data_train,
        aes(sample = 'residuals_01')
      )
      + stat_qq(alpha = 0.25)
      + stat_qq_line(color = 'red')
      + labs(
        title = 'Normality: Q-Q Plot',
        subtitle =
          'Points should follow the diagonal',
        x = 'Theoretical Quantiles',
        y = 'Sample Quantiles'
      )
    )
```


```{python}
# Identifiability
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor

predictors = [
      'log_price', 'brand_Jif', 'brand_Skippy',
      'brand_PeterPan', 'texture_Smooth', 'size_12'
    ]

X_train = snow_data.select(predictors)

pl.DataFrame({
      'predictor': predictors,
      'VIF': [
        variance_inflation_factor(X_train, i)
        for i in range(X_train.shape[1])
      ]
    })
```
